posts.summary: TIEZA sets the full Philippine travel tax at 1,620 pesos economy and 2,700 pesos first class in 2026, with short stay foreign visitors outside its scope.
posts.body:
Leaving Manila carries a Philippine travel tax of 1,620 pesos in economy and 2,700 pesos in first class in 2026, according to the Tourism Infrastructure and Enterprise Zone Authority, the government corporation that collects it. TIEZA describes the tax as a levy on individuals leaving the country, imposed under Presidential Decree 1183 as amended, regardless of where the air ticket was issued.

Who actually pays

TIEZA lists the payers of the full tax as citizens of the Philippines, taxable foreign passport holders, and non immigrant foreign passport holders who have stayed in the Philippines for more than one year. A visitor on a short tourist stay therefore falls outside the full travel tax.

Reduced rates and a worked example

The standard reduced tax is 810 pesos in economy and 1,350 in first class, and the privileged reduced rate for a dependent of an overseas Filipino worker is 300 pesos in economy. A family of four residents flying economy in 2026 pays 6,480 pesos at the full rate, or 3,240 pesos if all four qualify for the standard reduced rate.

What is still unclear

Whether the tax is already inside an airline fare or collected at a counter before departure varies by carrier, and TIEZA runs a separate refund process, so a passenger who was exempt but paid has to claim the money back afterwards.

Sources: TIEZA on the full travel tax and TIEZA travel tax rates.

posts.title: Marrakech tourist tax 2026: 10 to 25 dirhams per night in a five star hotel
posts.summary: Moroccan law bands the taxe de sejour at 10 to 25 dirhams per person per night for five star hotels and riads, and 15 to 30 for guesthouses and luxury hotels.
posts.body:
Morocco bands its taxe de sejour by law and lets each commune fix the exact figure inside the band. For a five star hotel the band is 10 to 25 dirhams per person per night, and for guesthouses, congress centres and luxury hotels it is 15 to 30 dirhams, in the local taxation law text published by the Treasury of the Kingdom of Morocco. Riads and houses let to tourists sit in the same 10 to 25 dirham band as five star hotels.

The rest of the scale

Four star hotels are 5 to 10 dirhams, three star 3 to 7, and one and two star 2 to 5. Tourist residences are 3 to 7 dirhams and holiday villages 5 to 10. The law says the tax is due per person and per night, comes on top of the room price, must be shown separately on the invoice, and is paid over to the commune quarterly. Children under 12 years are exempt.

A worked example

Two adults in a Marrakech riad for four nights face somewhere between 80 and 200 dirhams of tourist tax in 2026, depending on where inside the band the commune has set its rate. At the top of the band that is 200 dirhams, which on a modest riad is close to a full extra night.

What is still unclear

The national law fixes the bands, not the rate. The exact dirham figure applied in Marrakech is a communal decision that is not published in the national text, so the only reliable number for a given hotel is the one printed on its invoice.

Sources: Tresorerie Generale du Royaume, local taxation law text.

posts.title: Medellin hotel tax 2026: 0 percent IVA for foreign non residents against 19 percent
posts.summary: Colombia bills hotel stays by non resident foreign visitors at 0 percent IVA rather than the general 19 percent rate, on the tax authority own published doctrine.
posts.body:
A foreign visitor who is not resident in Colombia should be billed 0 percent IVA on a Medellin hotel room in 2026, rather than the general rate of 19 percent. The national tax authority DIAN states in its published doctrine that the general IVA rate is 19 percent under article 468 of the tax statute, and that hotel services to a non resident are invoiced at a rate of zero.

How the relief works

The exemption sits in article 481 of the tax statute, which covers tourist services supplied to residents abroad and used inside Colombia. DIAN notes that for hotel services the exemption applies regardless of whether the non resident guest or the travel agency pays the bill. The hotel has to verify and file documents showing the guest entered the country without the intention of settling there.

A worked example

Six nights at 400,000 pesos a night is 2,400,000 pesos. At 19 percent, IVA on that would be 456,000 pesos, and a qualifying non resident guest pays none of it. Medellin adds no separate nightly city tourist tax on top, so the room rate plus zero is the whole accommodation bill.

What is still unclear

The relief depends on the hotel being registered in the national tourism register and applying it properly. A guest whose passport details are not recorded at check in may still see 19 percent on the invoice and have to argue the point at the desk.

Sources: DIAN concept 3522 of 2025 on the tourist IVA exemption and DIAN concept 8922 of 2025 on the general 19 percent rate.

posts.title: Mexico City lodging tax 2026: 3.5 percent on hotels, 5 percent through platforms
posts.summary: Mexico City taxes accommodation at 3.5 percent, or 5 percent when a platform collects the payment for an apartment or house, under articles 162 to 164 of the city tax code.
posts.body:
Mexico City taxes accommodation at 3.5 percent of the amount charged in 2026, rising to 5 percent where an intermediary or platform collects the payment for an apartment or a house. Both rates are in articles 162 to 164 of the city tax code, in the text published by the city finance secretariat.

What counts as lodging

The code covers hotels, hostels, motels and timeshare, overnight areas for mobile accommodation such as campsites and caravan stops, and apartments and houses let in whole or in part. Lodging at hospitals, clinics, care homes, convents, seminaries and boarding schools is excluded. The code says the taxpayer passes the tax on to the guest, and the return is due by the fifteenth of the following month.

A worked example

Four nights in a hotel at 2,500 pesos a night is 10,000 pesos, and the lodging tax at 3.5 percent adds 350 pesos in 2026. The same 10,000 pesos booked as an apartment through a platform is taxed at 5 percent, or 500 pesos. Mexican value added tax applies separately on top of the room.

What is still unclear

Which rate applies turns on the property type and on whether the platform is the party collecting the money, and a booking page rarely spells that out, so a guest cannot easily tell in advance whether 3.5 or 5 percent is being charged.

Sources: Secretaria de Administracion y Finanzas de la Ciudad de Mexico, lodging tax articles of the city tax code.

posts.title: Milan tourist tax 2026: 12 euro per night in five star hotels from 1 April
posts.summary: Milan charges 12.00 euro per person per night in five star hotels from 1 April 2026 and 9.50 euro in short term rentals, per the Comune di Milano tourist tax page.
posts.body:
What the rate is

Milan charges 12.00 euro per person per night in five star hotels from 1 April 2026, according to the Comune di Milano's own tourist tax page. The city says resolution number 144 of 12 February 2026 redefined the rates for the whole of 2026 with effect from 1 April. The published schedule runs 3.00 euro for one star hotels, 4.00 euro for two star, 7.00 euro for three star, 10.00 euro for four star and 12.00 euro for five star. Accommodation outside the hotel category is listed separately: 9.50 euro for bed and breakfasts, holiday apartments and short term rentals under Legislative Decree 50/2017, 7.00 euro for holiday homes, and 3.00 euro for youth hostels and open air sites. The tax applies per person and per day of stay.

What a stay actually costs

Two people, four nights, one four star hotel. The rate is 10.00 euro per person per night, so the tax is 10.00 times 2 times 4, or 80 euro added to the room price. The same trip booked as a short term rental costs 9.50 times 2 times 4, which is 76 euro. In a three star hotel it is 56 euro, and in a hostel 24 euro.

Why 2026 has two schedules

An earlier schedule, approved by resolution 1418 of 13 November 2025 and in force from 1 January 2026, was lower at the top: 10.00 euro for both four and five star hotels and 7.40 euro for three star. What a traveller pays therefore depends on whether the stay falls before or after 1 April 2026. What the city page does not settle is whether the April schedule expires at the end of 2026.

Sources: Comune di Milano, Tourist tax: information.

posts.title: Montego Bay tourist taxes 2026: US$20 on arrival plus up to US$4 per room per night
posts.summary: Jamaica charges air arrivals a US$20 Tourism Enhancement Fee and hotels a Guest Accommodation Room Tax of up to US$4 per occupied room per night, per the Tourism Enhancement Fund and Tax Administration Jamaica.
posts.body:
The fee you pay on arrival

Every visitor flying into Jamaica pays US$20 in 2026. The Tourism Enhancement Fund, the government agency that collects the money, sets out on its own site that the 2017 amendment to the Tourism Enhancement Act provides for "A Tourism Enhancement Fee of US$20.00 to be charged to incoming airline passengers and US$2.00 to be charged to cruise passengers." Airlines collect it inside the ticket price, so most people landing at Sangster International never see it as a separate line.

The nightly room tax

Tax Administration Jamaica levies a Guest Accommodation Room Tax on every occupied room. Its published table gives US$1 for the smallest properties, US$2 for the middle band and US$4 for properties of "101 rooms and above", charged per room per night rather than per person. Most of the large Montego Bay resorts sit in the top band. The tax has applied since 1 September 2012, and the tax authority states that complimentary rooms attract it too.

A worked example

Two people, seven nights, one resort of more than 101 rooms. The room tax is US$4 times 7, which is US$28 for the room, not for each guest. Add the arrival fee of US$20 each and the fixed government charges for that trip come to US$68, before the general consumption tax that applies to the room rate itself.

One thing is genuinely unclear: the room bands as published overlap, listing 1 to 51 rooms and then 51 to 100 rooms, so a property with exactly 51 rooms is ambiguous on the page itself.

Sources: Tourism Enhancement Fund, Our Story and Tax Administration Jamaica, Guest Accommodation Room Tax.

posts.title: Munich tourist tax 2026: 0 euro, because Bavarian law bans the bed tax
posts.summary: Munich adds 0 euro per night in accommodation tax in 2026. Article 3 of the Bavarian Kommunalabgabengesetz names the Ubernachtungsteuer among local taxes that may not be levied.
posts.body:
The law is one sentence long

Munich adds 0 euro per night in city accommodation tax in 2026. Bavaria's Municipal Charges Act, the Kommunalabgabengesetz, settles it in a single line. Article 3 paragraph 3 reads: "Eine Getränkesteuer, eine Jagdsteuer, eine Speiseeissteuer, eine Übernachtungsteuer, eine Verpackungssteuer und eine Vergnügungssteuer dürfen nicht erhoben werden." An overnight tax sits on the list of local taxes that may not be levied, so no municipality in Bavaria, Munich included, can charge one.

What a stay costs

Four nights for two people in a Munich hotel adds 0 euro of accommodation tax, whatever the star rating and whatever the room rate. That is different from Berlin, Hamburg or Frankfurt, where a share of the room price is added. In Munich the only tax inside the room price is German value added tax, which hotels already include in the rate they quote.

Why travellers keep reading otherwise

The city has tried. DEHOGA Bayern, the state hospitality trade association, reported that Munich announced it would press ahead with an overnight tax and challenge the state government's decision, and that the state responded by widening article 3 of the Kommunalabgabengesetz so that an overnight tax is "in Bayern generell verboten". Booking sites and travel guides still list a Munich tourist tax, but the statute as published carries no rate at all.

What is unclear is whether litigation ever reopens this. The law on the books today allows no charge.

Sources: Bayerisches Kommunalabgabengesetz, Art. 3 and, as trade press, DEHOGA Bayern.

posts.title: Nairobi entry cost 2026: US$30 for Kenya's eTA, US$100 more to skip the wait
posts.summary: Kenya's Electronic Travel Authorisation starts at US$30 per traveller in 2026, with expedited processing costing an additional US$100, according to the official government eTA portal.
posts.body:
The fee

Kenya's Electronic Travel Authorisation costs US$30 in 2026. The official government eTA portal, run by the Directorate of Immigration Services, states in its FAQ that "Fees vary depending on the type of travel application selected with normal (processing may take up to 72 hours) starting at $30 and expedited (immediate processing) at an addition $100." A traveller who needs it the same day therefore pays US$130. There is no consular visa to buy separately; the eTA replaced the old visitor visa for most nationalities.

How long it takes

The same portal says that "Applications are generally processed within three (3) business days/72 hours but may take longer depending on the verification processes." The Directorate of Immigration Services repeats the three working day figure on its own site. That gap between three days and immediate is what the US$100 buys.

What a trip costs

Two adults flying into Jomo Kenyatta International for a Nairobi stay pay US$30 each, which is US$60 before a single night of accommodation. A family of four pays US$120. The portal lists a long set of exemptions, including citizens of East African Community partner states, who are admitted for up to 180 days without an eTA.

What is unclear is whether Nairobi County adds any local accommodation levy on top. The national eTA pages deal with entry only and say nothing about city level charges.

Sources: Republic of Kenya eTA, FAQs and Directorate of Immigration Services, eTA.

posts.title: Naples tourist tax 2026: 6.00 euro per night in four and five star hotels from 1 May
posts.summary: Naples charges 6.00 euro per person per night in four and five star hotels and in short term rentals from 1 May 2026, capped at 14 consecutive nights, per the Comune di Napoli.
posts.body:
The rates

Naples charges 6.00 euro per person per night in four star and five star hotels and in short term rentals from 1 May 2026, according to the Comune di Napoli's own imposta di soggiorno page. The schedule set by municipal resolution number 89 of 12 March 2026 reads: 6.00 euro for five star and five star luxury hotels, 6.00 euro for four star, 5.50 euro for three star, 4.50 euro for two star, 4.00 euro for one star, 5.50 euro for accommodation outside the hotel category and 6.00 euro for short term rentals. That is one euro above the rates the city applied at the start of the year.

How many nights you pay for

The city states that the tax "is paid per person and per overnight stay, up to a maximum of 14 consecutive days", so a long stay stops accruing after two weeks. Article 7 of the municipal regulation sets out the exemptions, which the page references rather than lists.

A worked example

Two people, five nights, a four star hotel in Naples in June 2026. The tax is 6.00 times 2 times 5, or 60 euro on top of the room price. The same stay in a three star hotel is 55 euro, in a one star hotel 40 euro, and booked as a short term rental 60 euro. A month long stay for one person in a four star hotel is capped at 14 nights, so 84 euro rather than 180 euro.

What is still unclear is the exact start date. The city says the increase takes effect on the first day of the second month after the act is published on the Ministry of Economy and Finance website, so 1 May depends on that publication holding.

Sources: Comune di Napoli, Imposta di Soggiorno 2026.

posts.title: Nassau hotel tax 2026: 10 percent VAT on the room and on the levies too
posts.summary: The Bahamas taxes hotel stays at the standard 10 percent VAT rate in 2026, and the Department of Inland Revenue confirms resort and promotion board levies sit inside the VAT base.
posts.body:
The rate

A Nassau hotel room is taxed at 10 percent in 2026. There is no separate hotel guest tax any more; value added tax replaced it. The Department of Inland Revenue states on its VAT page that "Two rates of VAT are applied which is the standard rate of 10% and a zero rate of 0%", and hotel accommodation falls under the standard rate.

The extras are taxed as well

This is where a Bahamas folio surprises people. The department's guidance on holiday accommodation and the tourism industry puts the surcharges inside the VAT base rather than outside it. It names administration and service charges, including mandatory service charges, and the resort levy, and says these "are also subject to VAT at the standard rate". On the promotion board levy it answers its own question directly: "Output VAT should be reported on promotion board levy as it forms part of the overall taxable income of the hotel." Energy surcharges, laundry and telephone are treated the same way.

A worked example

A room at US$300 per night for five nights is US$1,500. VAT at 10 percent is US$150. If the property adds US$100 of resort and promotion board levies across the stay, those are taxable too, adding US$10, so the bill carries US$160 of VAT on a US$1,600 base.

What is unclear is the size of those levies. The government guidance confirms they are taxable but does not publish their rates, and the copy of that guidance online still works its examples at the older 7.5 percent VAT rate.

Sources: Department of Inland Revenue, About VAT and VAT Guidance on Holiday Accommodation and the Tourism Industry.

posts.title: New Orleans hotel tax 2026: 15 percent combined plus 50 cents or a dollar per night
posts.summary: New Orleans hotels with 10 or more rooms carry a combined 15 percent tax, smaller properties 17 percent, plus an occupancy privilege tax of $0.50 or $1.00 per night, per the City of New Orleans.
posts.body:
The combined rate

A New Orleans hotel room is taxed at a combined 15 percent in 2026 when the property has 10 or more rooms, according to the City of New Orleans sales tax rate page. That figure is assembled from four separate charges: the Orleans Parish sales tax, the Louisiana state sales tax, the Louisiana Stadium and Exposition District room occupancy tax and the Ernest N. Morial Exhibition Hall Authority tax. Properties with 9 or fewer rooms are taxed at a combined 17 percent, because the state share on those is higher.

The flat nightly charge

On top of the percentage sits a Hotel Occupancy Privilege Tax, charged for each 24 hour period. The city lists it as $0.50 for hotels with 1 to 299 rooms, effective 7/1/2016, and $1.00 for hotels with 300 or more rooms. It is a per room charge, so a couple sharing pays it once.

A worked example

Four nights in a French Quarter hotel at $220 per night is $880 of room charges. At 15 percent the tax is $132. If that hotel has fewer than 300 rooms, add $0.50 for each of the four nights, which is $2.00. The government take is $134, or about 15.2 percent of the room rate. The same four nights in a nine room guest house would be taxed at 17 percent, which is $149.60, plus the same $2.00.

What the city page does not settle is whether any further tourism marketing district assessment applies to a given property, since that charge is not listed alongside the four it does name.

Sources: City of New Orleans, Orleans Parish sales tax rate.

posts.title: New York City hotel tax 2026: 5.875 percent plus $2.00 and $1.50 per night
posts.summary: New York City's hotel room occupancy tax is 5.875 percent, plus a flat $2.00 per room per night on most rooms and a $1.50 state hotel unit fee, before either sales tax.
posts.body:
Four charges, not one

New York City's hotel room occupancy tax is 5.875 percent of the rent. The Department of Finance describes it on its own page as "one of three taxes and one fee that apply to hotel room rentals in New York City": its own occupancy tax, New York State sales tax, New York City sales tax and the New York State Hotel Unit Fee of $1.50 per unit per day. Finance collects the first, the state collects the rest.

The flat city charge

The occupancy tax also carries a flat amount per room per day, set by rent band. Finance publishes it as 50 cents where the rent is $10 or more but less than $20, $1.00 from $20 to under $30, $1.50 from $30 to under $40, and $2.00 where the rent is $40 or more. Every realistic 2026 hotel room is in the top band, so assume $2.00 per room per night. A suite is charged $2.00 for each room in it.

A worked example

Three nights at $350 per night is $1,050 of room charges. The city occupancy tax at 5.875 percent is $61.69. Add $2.00 per night, which is $6.00, and the state hotel unit fee of $1.50 per night, which is $4.50. That is $72.19 in city and state hotel charges before either sales tax is applied to the same $1,050.

Anyone occupying a room for at least 180 consecutive days counts as a permanent resident and is exempt. What the Finance page leaves out is the two sales tax percentages: it names them and hands them to the state to publish.

Sources: NYC Department of Finance, Hotel room occupancy tax and New York State, Hotel and Motel Occupancy.

posts.title: Nice tourist tax 2026: 6.43 euro a night at the top, 2.28 euro in a three star hotel
posts.summary: Metropole Nice Cote d'Azur charges 6.43 euro per person per night for palaces and 2.28 euro for three star hotels from 1 January 2026, with unrated stays taxed at 6.70 percent capped at 6.43 euro.
posts.body:
The published rates

Nice charges 6.43 euro per person per night at the top of its scale in 2026. Métropole Nice Côte d'Azur, which has collected the tax since 2019, publishes a sheet headed "Tourist tax rates per person per night as from 1st January 2026". Every line is a metropolitan rate plus a 34 percent additional tax earmarked for the Ligne Nouvelle Provence Côte d'Azur rail project. Palaces are 4.80 plus 1.63, a total of 6.43 euro. Five star hotels, aparthotels and furnished rentals are 3.50 plus 1.19, a total of 4.69 euro. Four star is 2.60 plus 0.88, a total of 3.48 euro. Three star is 1.70 plus 0.58, a total of 2.28 euro.

Places with no star rating

Accommodation without a classification or awaiting one, which covers a great many apartments let to visitors, is charged 5 percent of the cost per person per night before tax, plus the additional 1.70 percent, so 6.70 percent in total. The sheet caps that at 6.43 euro, the palace rate.

A worked example

Two adults, six nights, a four star hotel near the Promenade. The tax is 3.48 times 2 times 6, which is 41.76 euro. The same trip in a three star hotel is 27.36 euro. In an unrated apartment at 90 euro per person per night before tax, the 6.70 percent rate gives 6.03 euro per person per night, still under the cap, so 72.36 euro for the stay.

The rate sheet is a rate sheet: it does not state which travellers are exempt, so that has to be checked separately with the métropole.

Sources: Métropole Nice Côte d'Azur, 2026 tourist tax rates.

posts.title: Oaxaca lodging tax 2026: 3 percent in hotels, 5 percent in apartments and houses
posts.summary: Oaxaca's reformed article 55 sets the lodging tax at 3 percent for hotels and 5 percent for apartments and houses used for lodging, the vacation rental category, from 2026.
posts.body:
Two rates from 2026

Oaxaca charges 3 percent on hotel lodging and 5 percent on lodging in apartments and houses. The reform to the Ley Estatal de Hacienda passed by the Congreso del Estado de Oaxaca rewrites article 55 so the tax is calculated "aplicando a la base, la tasa del 3 por ciento, para los supuestos establecidos en la fracción I del artículo 52", while for the cases in section II those collecting payment "deberán calcularlo aplicando la tasa del 5 por ciento".

Which category is which

Article 52 section I covers hotels, motels, hostels, inns, guest houses, cabins, bungalows, campsites and trailer parks, including timeshare. Section II covers "departamentos y casas utilizadas total o parcialmente para dicho fin", meaning apartments and houses used wholly or partly for lodging. That is the vacation rental category, and it now pays the higher rate. The law also places the collection duty on intermediaries, promoters and facilitators, which is how booking platforms are pulled in.

A worked example

Five nights in a hotel in Oaxaca city at 2,400 pesos per night is 12,000 pesos, and the lodging tax at 3 percent is 360 pesos. The same five nights in an apartment at 2,400 pesos per night is taxed at 5 percent, which is 600 pesos. On a two week stay the gap widens to 672 pesos against 1,120 pesos.

What is unclear is how consistently the platforms will apply the higher rate at the point of booking during 2026, and whether a listing shows it separately or folds it into the nightly price.

Sources: Congreso del Estado de Oaxaca, Ley Estatal de Hacienda.

posts.title: Osaka accommodation tax 2026: 200, 400 or 500 yen per person per night
posts.summary: Osaka Prefecture charges 200 yen per person per night from 5,000 yen, 400 yen from 15,000 yen and 500 yen from 20,000 yen, under rates that took effect on 1 September 2025.
posts.body:
The bands

Osaka Prefecture charges 200 yen per person per night when the room charge is 5,000 yen or more and under 15,000 yen, 400 yen from 15,000 to under 20,000 yen, and 500 yen at 20,000 yen and above. Below 5,000 yen there is no tax. The prefecture publishes this table on its own accommodation tax page and dates the current rates to 1 September 2025, so they apply throughout 2026. The schedule they replaced started at 7,000 yen and topped out at 300 yen, which is why older guides quote lower figures.

What counts as the room charge

The prefecture is explicit that the band is read off the accommodation charge per person per night, excluding breakfast and other service charges. A package rate therefore has to be stripped back to the room element before the band is chosen, which can drop a booking a band lower than the headline price suggests.

A worked example

Two people, four nights, a room at 24,000 yen per night for the two of them. That is 12,000 yen per person, so the first band applies: 200 yen each per night, or 1,600 yen for the stay. Move up to a room at 44,000 yen per night for two, which is 22,000 yen per person, and the tax becomes 500 yen each per night, or 4,000 yen for the same four nights.

What the prefecture page does not address is whether Osaka City layers anything on top; it describes a prefectural levy only.

Sources: Osaka Prefecture, accommodation tax and Osaka Prefecture tax office, shukuhakuzei.

posts.title: Paris tourist tax 2026: 15.93 euro a night in a palace, 8.45 euro in a four star hotel
posts.summary: From 1 January 2026 Paris charges 15.93 euro per adult per night in palaces, 11.70 euro in five star hotels and 8.45 euro in four star hotels, according to the city's tourist tax unit.
posts.body:
The 2026 tariff

Paris charges 15.93 euro per adult per night in a palace hotel and 8.45 euro in a four star hotel from 1 January 2026. The Ville de Paris tourist tax unit publishes the schedule under the heading "LES TARIFS DE LA TAXE DE SÉJOUR EN VIGUEUR À PARIS à partir du 1er janvier 2026". Each line is a municipal rate with three additions stacked on it: a departmental share of 10 percent, a regional share of 15 percent for the Société du Grand Paris and a further regional share of 200 percent for Ile de France Mobilités. For a four star hotel that is 2.60 plus 0.26 plus 0.39 plus 5.20, giving 8.45 euro. Five star works out at 11.70 euro and three star at 5.53 euro.

Unrated accommodation

Where a place has no classification or is waiting for one, the rate is 5 percent of the cost per person per night before tax, with the additional shares added, capped at 15.93 euro. The city spells out that the cost per person is the total nightly price divided by the number of travellers, minors included.

A worked example

Two adults, four nights, a four star hotel. The tax is 8.45 times 2 times 4, which is 67.60 euro on top of the room price. The same stay in a three star hotel is 44.24 euro, and in a five star hotel 93.60 euro. The 200 percent transport share alone accounts for 41.60 euro of that four star figure.

What is not obvious from the tariff sheet is how the Ile de France Mobilités share, by far the largest single component, is broken out on a hotel bill, if it is broken out at all.

Sources: Ville de Paris, tarifs de la taxe de séjour 2026 and the French government business portal.

posts.title: Petra entry fee 2026: 50 JOD for one day, 90 JOD if you do not sleep in Jordan
posts.summary: Petra charges 50 JOD for a one day ticket in 2026 if you spend at least one night in Jordan, and 90 JOD if you arrive and leave the same day, per the Jordan Tourism Board.
posts.body:
A one day ticket to Petra costs 50 Jordanian dinars in 2026 for a foreign visitor who spends at least one night in Jordan, according to the entrance fees table published by the Jordan Tourism Board. Two days costs 55 JOD and three days costs 60 JOD.

The day visitor price

The same table sets a separate price of 90 JOD for a one day visitor to Jordan, meaning someone who enters and leaves the country on the same date. That gap of 40 JOD is the largest single variable in the cost of seeing Petra, and your hotel booking decides it rather than the ticket desk.

What a real visit costs

Two adults on a two day ticket, both staying overnight in Wadi Musa, pay 55 JOD each, so 110 JOD in total at the gate. The same two adults arriving on a day trip and leaving Jordan that evening would pay 90 JOD each, or 180 JOD, for a shorter visit.

What is still unclear

The board publishes the prices without an effective date, so we cannot confirm from an official source when this schedule was last revised.

Sources: https://international.visitjordan.com/page/17/entrance-fees/

posts.title: Phuket hotel tax 2026: 7 percent VAT and no arrival fee yet
posts.summary: Thailand's Revenue Department puts VAT at 7 percent in 2026, the official arrival card is free, and the proposed 300 baht entry fee has been pushed back again.
posts.body:
Thailand charges 7 percent value added tax in 2026, and that is the only broad government tax on a Phuket hotel bill. The Revenue Department states on its own VAT page that "currently, the rate is 7 percent". No Thai government page sets out a separate nightly city or bed tax for Phuket.

The arrival card is free

Every foreign arrival files a Thailand Digital Arrival Card. The official site run by the Immigration Bureau titles itself "Official Thailand Digital Arrival Card (TDAC) No Fees Required", so the paperwork itself costs nothing.

The fee that keeps being delayed

The Nation, a Thai news outlet, reports that the Ministry of Tourism and Sports has pushed its planned entry charge of "300 baht for air arrivals and 150 baht for land or sea entries" to the second or third quarter of 2026. That is a news report about a pending change, not a tax in force.

What a stay costs

A room advertised at 4,000 baht per night for five nights comes to 20,000 baht, and 7 percent VAT adds 1,400 baht. Hotels commonly add a service charge as well, which is a private charge and not a tax. Whether the 300 baht fee actually starts during 2026 is not settled on any official page.

Sources: https://www.rd.go.th/english/6043.html and https://tdac.immigration.go.th/ and https://www.nationthailand.com/news/tourism/40052562

posts.title: Porto tourist tax 2026: 3 euros per person per night, capped at 7 nights
posts.summary: Porto charges 3 euros per guest per night in 2026, for a maximum of seven consecutive nights, with guests aged 12 or under exempt, according to the city council.
posts.body:
Porto charges a municipal tourist tax of 3 euros per guest per night in 2026, up to a maximum of seven consecutive nights. The city council's own leaflet states that the value of the tax is "3 euros por dormida, ate um maximo de 7 (sete) noites seguidas". The current rate took effect on 1 December 2024 under the new municipal regulation.

Who does not pay

The council lists exemptions for children and young people aged 12 or under, for stays caused by a medical procedure with up to two companions, for people with a disability of 60 percent or more with two companions, for pilgrims on their first night in a pilgrim hostel in the city, and for asylum seekers temporarily displaced from their home countries. Proof is required in every case.

What a stay costs

Two adults on a four night city break pay 3 euros each per night, so 24 euros added to the bill. A couple staying ten nights pays for seven nights only, which is 42 euros rather than 60. Hotels and registered short term rentals both collect it.

What is still unclear

The council has discussed raising the tax to 4 euros, but no official page we found sets a date, so 3 euros is the figure to budget for.

Sources: https://atividadeseconomicas.cm-porto.pt/alojamento-local/taxa-municipal-turistica-do-porto and https://taxaturistica.cm-porto.pt/Content/documents/tmt_folhetos_PT.pdf

posts.title: Prague accommodation fee 2026: 50 CZK per person per night
posts.summary: Prague charges 50 CZK per person for each started day of a stay except the day of arrival in 2026, under city ordinance number 19/2021.
posts.body:
Prague charges 50 Czech crowns per person per night in 2026. Prague 1, the district that administers the fee across much of the historic centre, gives the rate as 50 crowns "za kazdy zapocaty den, krome dne prijezdu", meaning for each started day of the stay except the day of arrival. In practice that works out at one charge per night slept.

Where it comes from

The district cites city ordinance number 19/2021 on the local fee from stay. It applies to a paid stay lasting at most 60 consecutive days with the same provider, so hotels, hostels, guest houses and short term rentals all collect it.

Who is exempt

The district lists people under 18, blind people, holders of a ZTP/P card, hospital patients, seasonal workers and students in educational facilities among those who do not pay.

What a stay costs

Two adults arriving on a Monday and leaving on the Friday are charged for four days each, so eight chargeable days at 50 CZK, which is 400 CZK on top of the room rate and its VAT. Whether Prague raises the rate later in 2026 is not stated on any city page we found.

Sources: https://www.praha1.cz/potrebuji-si-vyridit/odbory/poplatek-z-pobytu/

posts.title: Punta Cana tourist card 2026: 10 US dollars, already inside your airfare
posts.summary: The Dominican tourist card costs 10 US dollars in 2026 and has been built into air and sea ticket prices since a 2017 decree, according to the tax authority's own general norm.
posts.body:
Entering the Dominican Republic as a tourist costs 10 US dollars in 2026, and you almost certainly paid it when you bought the flight. The tax authority's General Norm 08 of 2018 describes the collection of "los diez dolares de los Estados Unidos de America con 00/100 (US$10.00)" for the tourist card.

Why you never see it

The same norm records that a decree of 4 December 2017 ordered the tourist card charge to be incorporated into the price of air and sea tickets for tourists arriving by those routes. Passengers arriving in transit by air or sea, and those transferring to cruise ships, are excluded from it.

Who can claim it back

The norm exists partly to set out a refund procedure for people who were charged but should not have been. The tax authority asks for a passport copy and evidence of the charge, and the claim is made online.

What a trip costs

A family of four flying into Punta Cana pays 40 US dollars in tourist card charges, spread invisibly across four fares. What a resort adds at check in for local sales tax and service is a separate matter, and we could not confirm those percentages on a Dominican government page.

Sources: https://www.puntacanainternationalairport.com/images/imagenes/servicios/pdf/norma-08-18.pdf

posts.title: Queenstown visitor levy 2026: NZD 100, plus an NZeTA from NZD 17
posts.summary: Most visitors to Queenstown pay New Zealand's International Visitor Conservation and Tourism Levy of NZD 100 in 2026, plus an NZeTA priced from NZD 17.
posts.body:
New Zealand charges an International Visitor Conservation and Tourism Levy of NZD 100 in 2026, and almost everyone flying into Queenstown pays it. Immigration New Zealand states that "many tourists, people on working holidays, and some students and workers coming to New Zealand must pay an International Visitor Conservation and Tourism Levy (IVL) of NZD $100".

The travel authority on top

Most visa waiver travellers also need an NZeTA. Immigration New Zealand prices it "From NZD $17" and says it is valid for two years for travellers and five years for airline crew. The levy is normally paid at the same time as the request.

Who does not pay

The department says you do not pay the levy if you travel on an Australian or New Zealand passport, or a passport from many Pacific Island nations, and it exempts transit passengers, resident visa holders and business visitor visa holders. It also warns that "we do not refund the IVL, even if we decline your application".

What a trip costs

A couple arriving for a week in Queenstown pays NZD 200 in levy plus at least NZD 34 for two NZeTAs, so NZD 234 before a single night of accommodation. Whether Queenstown adds a bed tax of its own during 2026 is not settled on any official page we found.

Sources: https://www.immigration.govt.nz/process-to-apply/applying-for-a-visa/fees-processing-times-and-refunds/paying-the-international-visitor-levy/ and https://www.immigration.govt.nz/new-zealand-visas/visas/visa/nzeta

posts.title: Reykjavik accommodation tax 2026: 800 ISK per night plus 11 percent VAT
posts.summary: Iceland's lodging tax is 800 ISK per night for hotels and guesthouses in 2026, and accommodation carries the reduced 11 percent VAT rate, per Iceland Revenue and Customs.
posts.body:
A night in a Reykjavik hotel carries a lodging tax of 800 Icelandic kronur in 2026. Iceland Revenue and Customs lists "800 kr./lodging tax unit" for hotels, guesthouses and similar operations holding a licence in the higher categories, and states that the current amounts apply from 1 January 2025.

Campsites and cruise berths

The same table sets 400 kronur per unit for camp sites and parking spots for motorhomes, trailers, pop up campers and caravan sites, and 400 kronur for cruise ships on domestic voyages. The tax is a flat amount per unit sold, so it does not rise with the room price.

VAT sits on top

The tax authority puts the standard rate at 24 percent and states that "the reduced rate of VAT in Iceland is 11% and applies to the sales of following goods and services: Rental of hotel and guestrooms". Cottages, fishing lodges and hostels also fall under 11 percent when the rent period is under one month.

What a stay costs

Five nights in a Reykjavik guesthouse adds 4,000 kronur of lodging tax on top of the room rate and its 11 percent VAT. Whether the government raises the lodging tax again during 2026 is not stated on the tax authority page.

Sources: https://www.skatturinn.is/english/companies/tax-issues/lodging-tax/ and https://www.skatturinn.is/english/companies/value-added-tax/

posts.title: Rome tourist tax 2026: 4 to 10 euros per person per night, capped at 10 nights
posts.summary: Rome's contributo di soggiorno runs from 4 euros a night in a one star hotel to 10 euros in a five star in 2026, for at most 10 consecutive nights, per the city's own tariff table.
posts.body:
Rome charges between 4 and 10 euros per person per night in 2026. The tariff table published by Roma Capitale lists a one star hotel at "Euro 4,00", two stars at 5,00 euros, three stars at 6,00 euros, four stars at 7,50 euros and "Albergo a 5 stelle o a maggiore classificazione" at "Euro 10,00". Every hotel line carries a maximum of 10 nights.

Outside hotels

The same table sets 6,00 euros for bed and breakfasts, agriturismi, country houses, category 1 holiday apartments and property let on short lets, 5,00 euros for category 2 holiday apartments, 3,50 euros for hostels and mountain refuges, and 3,00 euros for campsites and camper areas, where the cap falls to 5 nights.

What a stay costs

Two adults spending four nights in a four star hotel pay 7,50 euros each per night, so 60 euros on top of the room rate. The cap matters on longer trips: a couple staying 14 nights in a three star pays for 10 nights each at 6,00 euros, which is 120 euros rather than 168.

What is still unclear

The official table is the one issued for stays from 1 October 2023, and we found no city page announcing a revision for 2026.

Sources: https://www.comune.roma.it/web-resources/cms/documents/Nuove_tariffe_contributo_di_soggiorno_dal_01.10.2023_logo.pdf

posts.title: Costa Rica air entry tax 2026: 15 US dollars on a ticket bought abroad
posts.summary: The Costa Rican Tourism Board lists a 15 US dollar tax for entering Costa Rica by air on a ticket bought abroad in 2026, alongside two separate 5 percent taxes on international tickets.
posts.body:
Flying into San Jose on a ticket bought outside Costa Rica carries a tax of 15 US dollars in 2026. The Costa Rican Tourism Board, the government body that administers it, lists "a $15.00 tax for entering Costa Rica by air, with a ticket acquired abroad" and attributes it to Law number 8694 of 11 December 2008.

Two more ticket taxes

The same board administers "a 5% tax on tickets sold in Costa Rica, for any kind of international travel" under a 1955 law, and a 5 percent tax on tickets with Costa Rica as the country of origin under the 2008 law. Both reach you through the airline rather than at an airport counter.

What a trip costs

Two people flying in from abroad carry 30 US dollars of entry tax inside their fares. A 600 dollar international ticket bought in Costa Rica carries a further 30 dollars under the 5 percent rule, again inside the fare rather than as a separate line at the airport.

What is still unclear

Travel sites widely quote a 29 US dollar departure tax at San Jose, but no Costa Rican government page we could reach in 2026 states that figure, so treat it as unconfirmed.

Sources: https://www.ict.go.cr/en/our-work/revenue-department.html

posts.title: Santorini cruise fee 2026: 20 euros per passenger from June to September
posts.summary: Greek law sets a cruise disembarkation fee of 20 euros per passenger at Santorini and Mykonos from 1 June to 30 September in 2026, falling to 12 euros either side and 4 euros in winter.
posts.body:
Stepping off a cruise ship at Santorini costs 20 euros per passenger between 1 June and 30 September in 2026. Article 27 of Law 5162 of 2024, printed in the Government Gazette issue of 5 December 2024, sets the cruise fee for disembarkation at ports of the islands of Mykonos and Santorini at twenty euros for that period.

The rest of the year

The same article sets 12 euros for Santorini and Mykonos from 1 to 31 October and from 1 April to 31 May, and 4 euros from 1 November to 31 March. Every other Greek port charges 5 euros, 3 euros and 1 euro across those same three periods. The fee falls on the passenger, applies per port, and carries no VAT.

If you sleep on the island

Hotel guests pay something different. Article 24 of the same law sets the climate crisis resilience fee per room per day from April to October at 2 euros for one and two star hotels, 5 euros for three star, 10 euros for four star and 15 euros for five star. From November to March those drop to 0,50, 1,50, 3 and 4 euros.

What a visit costs

Two cruise passengers landing in July pay 40 euros between them. A couple spending four July nights in a four star hotel pay 40 euros of resilience fee on the room. The Greek tax authority's own guidance page refused every request we made, so we could not cross check the law text against it.

Sources: https://www.grhotels.gr/telos-anthektikotitas-stin-klimatiki-krisi-kai-alles-forologikes-diatakseis/

posts.title: Bali tourist levy 2026: 150,000 rupiah per person
posts.summary: Foreign visitors to Bali pay a levy of 150,000 rupiah in 2026, paid through the official Love Bali portal under Bali Provincial Regulation Number 2 of 2025.
posts.body:
Every foreign tourist arriving in Bali pays 150,000 rupiah in 2026. The provincial government's own Love Bali site shows the amount as "IDR 150,000" on its payment form and names the legal basis as "Bali Provincial Regulation Number 2 of 2025 Amendment to Regional Regulation Number 6 of 2023 concerning the Levy for International Tourists for the Protection of Balinese Culture and Natural Environment".

How it is paid

Payment runs through the Love Bali portal or its app, before arrival or on the day, and produces a voucher to show at a checkpoint. The site runs a payment check that looks for a previous transaction with the same name, passport number, country and arrival date, which is how it avoids charging the same traveller twice.

What a Seminyak trip costs

A family of four staying in Seminyak pays 600,000 rupiah in total, once, whether they stay four nights or fourteen. The amount does not vary by where on the island you sleep, and the portal also carries an exemption route.

What is still unclear

The portal does not state on its front page whether a traveller who leaves Bali and returns within the same trip has to pay a second time, so budget for one payment per arrival.

Sources: https://lovebali.baliprov.go.id/

posts.title: Seoul entry cost 2026: the 10,000 won travel authorization is waived all year
posts.summary: South Korea's electronic travel authorization costs 10,000 won, but nationals of the currently exempt countries need none at all between 1 January and 31 December 2026.
posts.body:
The Korea Electronic Travel Authorization costs 10,000 won, and for most visitors to Seoul in 2026 it costs nothing at all, because the exemption has been extended for another full year. The official application portal lists the fee as 10,000 won and says review normally takes up to 72 hours.

The waiver runs all year

A notice published by a Korean diplomatic mission sets the extension "From January 1, 2026 (Thursday) to December 31, 2026 (Thursday) (KST)" and states that the countries and regions currently exempt, including the United States, are covered by it. Exempt travellers are shown a message telling them no authorization is needed.

You can still apply

The same notice says those who want the benefits of an approval may apply anyway, and "in that case, the application fee will be charged". That is a choice rather than a requirement, and the fee is not refunded.

What a trip costs

Two travellers from an exempt country pay nothing to enter Seoul in 2026. The same two applying voluntarily would pay 20,000 won between them. What happens after 31 December 2026 is not settled, since the waiver has been renewed a year at a time and no page states a permanent policy.

Sources: https://www.k-eta.go.kr/portal/apply/index.do and https://usa.mofa.go.kr/us-newyork-en/brd/m_25545/view.do?seq=21

posts.title: Singapore hotel tax 2026: 9 percent GST on the room rate
posts.summary: Singapore's goods and services tax stands at 9 percent in 2026 according to the Ministry of Finance, so a 300 dollar room carries 27 dollars of tax a night.
posts.body:
The rate

Singapore's goods and services tax is 9 percent in 2026, and that is the government tax a visitor meets on a hotel bill. The Ministry of Finance sets out the history on its own goods and services tax page: the rate began at 3 percent in 1994, moved to 7 percent in 2007, then to 8 percent in 2023 and 9 percent in 2024. Nothing later appears on that page, so 9 percent is the figure that applies through 2026.

What a stay costs

Take a room advertised at 300 Singapore dollars per night. GST at 9 percent adds 27 dollars, so one night is 327 dollars. Four nights is 1,200 dollars of room rate and 108 dollars of tax, for a total of 1,308 dollars. On a two week trip at that price the tax alone reaches 378 dollars, which is worth building into a budget rather than discovering at the desk.

What sits beside it

Singapore has no separate nightly bed charge listed alongside GST on the ministry page, so unlike Vienna or Amsterdam there is no percentage stacked on top of the consumption tax. Most hotels do add a service charge of their own, but that is a business decision rather than a rate set by the tax authority.

What we could not settle from a primary source is exactly how a hotel service charge is treated for GST purposes, so the final line on a Singapore bill can sit above the 9 percent worked out here.

Sources: mof.gov.sg.

posts.title: Stockholm hotel tax 2026: 12 percent Swedish VAT on the room
posts.summary: Skatteverket puts VAT on hotel room rentals at 12 percent in 2026, so an 1,800 krona net rate becomes 2,016 kronor. No separate nightly city levy appears on the agency rate list.
posts.body:
The rate

Hotel rooms in Sweden carry 12 percent value added tax in 2026, according to Skatteverket, the Swedish tax agency. Its page on VAT rates and exemptions says a business should normally charge 12 percent on room rentals in hotel, guest house and hostel operations or similar. The same reduced rate covers services tied closely to the room. Conference arrangements are charged at 25 percent instead, which is why a meeting package and a bed can be taxed differently in the same building.

What a stay costs

Take a room at 1,800 kronor a night before tax. VAT at 12 percent adds 216 kronor, so one night is 2,016 kronor. Four nights is 7,200 kronor of room rate plus 864 kronor of tax, or 8,064 kronor in total. Where a price is already quoted with tax inside, the same 12 percent is sitting in the number rather than being added later.

No separate city levy

The agency rate list is where a Swedish accommodation charge would appear, and it shows only the 12 percent rate on room rentals, with no per person nightly visitor fee of the kind several European capitals collect.

What that source cannot settle on its own is whether any Stockholm specific charge exists outside the national VAT system, since the page covers national rates rather than municipal decisions.

Sources: skatteverket.se.

posts.title: Sydney departure tax 2026: 70 Australian dollars per person
posts.summary: Australian law sets the Passenger Movement Charge at 70 dollars for each departure, so a family of four leaving Sydney in 2026 carries 280 dollars of it inside their fares.
posts.body:
The charge

Leaving Australia costs 70 Australian dollars a person in 2026. It is not a Sydney levy and not a hotel tax. It is federal, and the number sits in the Passenger Movement Charge Act 1978, which states that the rate of charge imposed by the Act in respect of the departure of a person from Australia is 70 dollars. The compilation published on the Federal Register of Legislation is the authority for that figure.

Where you actually pay it

You will rarely see it on its own line. Airlines and shipping operators collect the charge when the ticket is sold and pass it to the Commonwealth, so for most visitors it is folded into the taxes and fees component of an international fare out of Sydney rather than presented at the airport.

What a trip costs

Two adults flying out of Sydney carry 140 dollars of Passenger Movement Charge inside their fares. A family of four carries 280 dollars. On a two week trip where most other costs move with the season, this is one line fixed by statute rather than by an airline, which makes it easy to budget exactly.

What the Act does not settle is how each carrier displays the charge in a fare breakdown, so the amount may appear bundled with airport and security fees rather than shown separately.

Sources: legislation.gov.au.

posts.title: Tokyo accommodation tax 2026: 100 or 200 yen per person per night
posts.summary: The Tokyo Metropolitan Government charges 100 yen a night per person for rooms from 10,000 to under 15,000 yen and 200 yen at 15,000 yen and above. Cheaper rooms pay nothing.
posts.body:
The rate

Tokyo's accommodation tax in 2026 is either 100 yen or 200 yen per person per night, depending on the room rate. The Bureau of Taxation of the Tokyo Metropolitan Government lists the bands on its accommodation tax page for guests: 100 yen where the charge is 10,000 yen or more but under 15,000 yen, and 200 yen where it is 15,000 yen or more. Below 10,000 yen per person per night nothing is due at all.

What a stay costs

Two people in a room billed at 22,000 yen per person per night for five nights fall in the upper band. That is 200 yen each per night, so 1,000 yen each and 2,000 yen for the pair across the stay. A hostel bed at 9,000 yen a night adds nothing. Even at the top band the tax is small against Tokyo room rates, which is the honest summary: this is a rounding error, not a budget item.

The 2027 change

The same official page carries a note that the rules change from 1 April 2027 and move away from the flat bands. For any stay falling inside 2026 the two amounts above are what applies.

What the guest page does not spell out is how the tax is handled on package rates that bundle meals, so the taxable room portion of a package may not be obvious on the bill.

Sources: tax.metro.tokyo.lg.jp, tax.metro.tokyo.lg.jp.

posts.title: Vancouver hotel tax 2026: 8 percent PST plus up to 5.5 percent in levies
posts.summary: British Columbia charges 8 percent PST on short term accommodation, up to 3 percent municipal and regional district tax, and a further 2.5 percent Major Events tax in Vancouver until 2030.
posts.body:
The three layers

A Vancouver hotel room carries three provincial charges in 2026. The Province of British Columbia sets them out on its own accommodation tax page: PST of 8 percent applies to sales of short term accommodation in the province unless a specific exemption applies, a municipal and regional district tax of up to 3 percent applies in participating areas, and an additional Major Events tax applies to short term accommodation in the City of Vancouver, effective 1 February 2023 until 31 January 2030, at 2.5 percent.

What a stay costs

Take a room at 300 dollars a night for three nights, so 900 dollars of room rate. PST at 8 percent is 72 dollars. The district tax at the full 3 percent is 27 dollars. The Major Events tax at 2.5 percent is 22.50 dollars. That is 121.50 dollars of accommodation tax, or 13.5 percent on top of the rate, before any federal tax is added to the bill.

The end date

The 2.5 percent Major Events layer is temporary by design, and the province gives 31 January 2030 as its expiry, so it is in force for every night of 2026.

What the provincial page leaves open is the exact district tax rate in force for Vancouver, since it states a ceiling of 3 percent rather than a city by city figure.

Sources: www2.gov.bc.ca, www2.gov.bc.ca.

posts.title: Vienna Ortstaxe 2026: 5 percent of the net room rate from 1 July
posts.summary: Vienna's local tax rose from 3.2 percent to 5 percent of the net accommodation charge on 1 July 2026, with a further step to 8 percent already scheduled for July 2027.
posts.body:
The rate

Vienna charges 5 percent Ortstaxe on overnight stays from 1 July 2026. The City of Vienna publishes the schedule in its own official guidance: 3.2 percent of the charge for the stay, excluding VAT and breakfast and after a flat deduction of 11 percent, applied until 30 June 2026; from 1 July 2026 until 30 June 2027 the rate is 5 percent of the charge for the stay, excluding VAT and breakfast; and from 1 July 2027 it becomes 8 percent. The flat 11 percent deduction belongs to the old rate only.

What a stay costs

Say the accommodation charge is 160 euro a night once VAT and breakfast are stripped out. Ortstaxe at 5 percent is 8 euro a night. Four nights adds 32 euro to the bill. The same stay before 1 July 2026 would have carried roughly 4.60 euro a night once the old rate and its 11 percent deduction were applied, so the increase is close to a doubling in practice.

What changes next

The 8 percent step is already in the published schedule for 1 July 2027, so an identical room booked next summer will cost more again. The hotel collects the tax and passes it to the city.

What the city page does not resolve for a traveller is how a hotel splits a rate that bundles breakfast, since only the accommodation part is taxable.

Sources: wien.gv.at, wien.gv.at.

posts.title: Zanzibar infrastructure tax 2026: 1 to 5 US dollars per person per night
posts.summary: The Zanzibar Revenue Board charges hotel guests between 1 and 5 US dollars per person per day depending on the hotel star rating, collected at the property rather than at booking.
posts.body:
The tax

Hotel guests in Zanzibar pay an infrastructure tax of 1 to 5 US dollars per person per day in 2026. The Zanzibar Revenue Board describes it on its own infrastructure tax page as a tax collected and allocated to infrastructure services in Zanzibar, and gives the hotel rate as ranging from 1 to 5 dollars per person per day depending on the hotel star rate. Rooms located underwater are charged separately at 10 dollars per person per day.

What a stay costs

Two people spending seven nights at a property charged at the top of the band pay 5 dollars each a night, so 70 dollars across the stay. At the bottom of the band the same trip costs 14 dollars. Either way it is settled at the property, in cash or on the final bill, and it is added to a room rate that may already have been paid in full at booking.

Where it comes from

The revenue board lists the legal basis as the Infrastructure Tax 2015, consolidated in 2025, alongside the Tax Administration and Procedures Act of 2009. The same tax also falls on diesel and petrol at 100 shillings a litre and on electricity at 2 percent, so the hotel line is one part of a wider levy.

What the board does not publish on that page is which star rating maps to which dollar amount, so the exact nightly figure for a given hotel is only knowable from the hotel itself.

Sources: zanrevenue.org, zanrevenue.org.
